# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual but cannot speak, and I can only gesture to Deaf. Blind is the one who needs the wire color to cut, but I can't reach Blind directly - I can only communicate through Deaf, who speaks after me... wait, actually the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so Blind speaks before Deaf but after me in this round. I can't send anything Blind receives directly since I can only gesture to Deaf.

I need to wait until I know what display number and light color are showing, which only Deaf can see. I have no information yet to send. Let me wait this turn and see what comes in from Blind and Deaf next round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows the number 3. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is blue. Waiting for manual guidance before any wire is touched.

Deaf saw display=3, light=green. From my manual, row 3, column green = red. So the correct wire to cut is the red wire.

Deaf speaks after me and can see my gestures. I need to tell Deaf "red" so Deaf can then relay it to Blind (since Blind cannot see gestures, and I cannot speak to Blind directly). I'll use a gesture that Deaf can interpret as pointing to the red wire — but gestures carry no inherent meaning until established. I should establish a simple convention: since Deaf already told us wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is blue, I can gesture the wire number.

I'll use ☝ for "wire 1" to indicate the first wire, which is red - matching the answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 3, light green, wires red green blue in order 1 2 3. Gesture which wire number is safe using pointing symbols, one at a time.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf understood my gesture as "wire 1" and is echoing it back for confirmation, asking me to confirm using pointing symbols. Display 3 + green light = red wire per manual, which is wire 1 (Deaf said wire 1 is red). My previous gesture ☝ already indicated wire 1. Deaf seems to want explicit confirmation this round.

I'll confirm with ☝ again so Deaf is certain, and Deaf can then relay this to Blind since Deaf speaks after me and Blind comes right after Deaf... wait, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So within this round, Blind already spoke before me, and Deaf speaks after me. Deaf will need to relay the answer to Blind next round via speech, since Blind can hear Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Received your one-finger sign twice, I think you mean wire number 1. If wire 1 is correct reply again with one finger. If wire 2, use two fingers. If wire 3, three fingers.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf has correctly interpreted my signal as wire 1, and is asking for one more confirmation with the same convention. This matches the manual: display 3, light green → red, and wire 1 is red. I'll confirm once more with a single finger to lock this in before Deaf relays it to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind and can only cut wires by position 1, 2, or 3. I need to know from the manual what condition determines which wire to cut. Deaf has already reported the colors and display to you if you are receiving their gestures - please tell me the rule.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak, so Blind cannot receive anything from me directly - only Deaf can hear Blind and me... wait, actually I cannot speak at all, only gesture, and gestures only reach Deaf (who can see). Blind cannot see gestures. So I truly cannot communicate with Blind directly.

Deaf has confirmed receiving my signal (☝ 👍 = wire 1, confirmed). Deaf needs to be the one who tells Blind "cut wire 1" via speech, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear. My job is done for this specific case - I already confirmed wire 1 to Deaf twice. I should reinforce this one more time to make sure Deaf relays it, since Deaf's message shows they now have it clearly (☝👍 acknowledgment).

I have nothing new to add; Deaf has the answer and needs to relay to Blind by speech.

```
wait()
```
